name: Token price

subjectOf.text: An issuer can pre-define monetary policy in crypto economics by fixing the number of tokens created and issued, and a maximum token issuance combined with controlled token supply releases can make small increases in demand drive token prices higher.
subjectOf.abstract: A maximum token issuance in combination with controlled token supply releases can result in small increases in demand driving token prices higher.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: token issuances with a predetermined maximum supply

subjectOf.text: Combining quasi-fiscal policy, increasing benefits attached to tokens, with monetary policy, increasing supply in circulation, may or may not have an effect on the market price of the tokens.
subjectOf.abstract: The combined effect of quasi-fiscal policy (increasing benefits associated with the tokens) and monetary policy (increasing the token supply in circulation) may or may not have an effect on the market price of the respective tokens.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Crypto Economics - The Top 100 Token Models Compared (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3249860
scope_conditions: when benefit increases and supply increases are applied simultaneously

subjectOf.text: Under a deflationary token model, prices are expected to increase because of the fundamental scarcity of token supply.
subjectOf.abstract: With a deflationary method, prices are expected to increase due to fundamental scarcity of token supply.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Crypto Economics - The Top 100 Token Models Compared (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3249860
scope_conditions: tokens with a capped maximum issuance
